analysis.headline: House Passes Sunshine Protection Act to Make Daylight Saving Time Permanent
analysis.summary: The U.S. House of Representatives passed the Sunshine Protection Act of 2025 on Tuesday by a vote of 308-117, which would make daylight saving time the permanent standard time nationwide and eliminate the twice-yearly clock change. The bill, backed by President Donald Trump and sponsored by Rep. Vern Buchanan (R-FL), now heads to the Senate for consideration. The U.S. Senate unanimously passed a similar measure in 2022 — the original Sunshine Protection Act — only for it to die in the House, illustrating how this perennially popular idea has repeatedly stalled in the legislative process. Whether to make daylight saving or standard time permanent also carries significant public health implications, as research links permanent standard time more closely to human circadian biology, putting scientific consensus and legislative preference on a potential collision course.
